name: Mint Turquoise
lede: Mint Turquoise is a muted blue-green standardized as RAL 6033, a paint color shared with the stone that gives turquoise its name.

sections.title: A standardized paint color
sections.body:
Our library gives this color's primary source as RAL Classic, catalog number 6033, a German paint-matching standard founded in 1927, so the hex is an approximate screen value of a printed color card [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately lists a related name, Pacifie, first recorded in 1918, plate 36 J 1 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[porcelain-green]] and [[mint-turquoise]], at 
The nearest library neighbor is Dusty Teal [1]. Compare [[aquamarine|Aquamarine]] and [[mint|Mint]], two other pale colors it sits between [1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[skobeloff-green]], 4.8 ΔE away, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a color within six units of this one in 26, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [2]. It covers the most canvas in Gustave Caillebotte's 1877 Skiffs and Édouard Manet's 1864 Sea View, Calm Weather, both paintings of open water [2]. It turns up about 13 times more often in Impressionist paintings than in the archive overall, consistent with the period's taste for pale sea and sky color [2]. These are matches in photographed, varnished paintings, not a claim that RAL 6033 paint was used [2].
